findings.summary: PLANS 9.3 status, the changelog 9.3 entry, and the worker report describe the truncation as '512/256'; the actual pinned ActivityLog bounds are Name/Overview/ShortOverview 512 and Type 256 (ADR-021 states this correctly), and the code truncates to those bounds.
findings.detail: The pinned entity (src/Jellyfin.Database/Jellyfin.Database.Implementations/Entities/ActivityLog.cs) and the SQLite migration (20200514181226_AddActivityLog.cs) bound Name/Overview/ShortOverview to 512 and Type to 256. JellyfinConfigurationRejectionNotifier uses MaxFieldLength=512 for Overview and ShortOverview, a fixed 30-char Name, a fixed 29-char Type, and MaxReasonLength=256, so every written field is within the real column bounds. ADR-021 clause 3 states the bounds precisely ('Name/Overview/ShortOverview 512, Type 256'). The '512/256' shorthand in PLANS/changelog/worker-report can be read as 'ShortOverview 256', which is not the bound, but it is a phrasing imprecision rather than a correctness defect, and it is not a current-state status surface.
findings.recommended_action: Optional wording cleanup in a later docs pass; no code or decision change required.

findings.summary: The PLANS 9.3 formal 'Acceptance criteria' line was not amended to name administrator surfacing (AR-01's recommended rework), although the Objective, Work, Tests, Status, ADR-021, and the implementation all require and satisfy it.
findings.detail: AR-01 recommended_action included 'update the 9.3 completion criteria so administrator surfacing is required and testable'. The rework updated the 9.3 Status (which explicitly requires 'surfaced to the administrator as exactly one bounded, secret-free activity-log entry'), the Objective ('the bounded validation failure is surfaced to the administrator'), the Work bullet ('surface the bounded, secret-free validation failure'), and the Tests line ('the validation failure is surfaced safely'), and added a test that asserts exactly one bounded secret-free entry on rejection. Only the terse 'Acceptance criteria:' sentence still reads 'an invalid change is rejected and the last valid snapshot is retained' without naming surfacing. The substantive completion criteria are therefore covered; the omission is a documentation-completeness nit, not an unmet requirement.

findings.summary: base.UpdateConfiguration is not wrapped, so a failure inside the host's own base method propagates unchanged; this preserves the host's pre-existing behavior and is documented, and every plugin-added path is contained.
findings.detail: The override calls base.UpdateConfiguration(configuration) outside a try/catch. The base implementation (pinned MediaBrowser.Common/Plugins/BasePluginOfT.cs) does Configuration = candidate; SaveConfiguration; ConfigurationChanged?.Invoke, and its own ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(configuration) is mirrored by the override. A host base failure (e.g., an I/O failure in SaveConfiguration) therefore propagates exactly as it would without the override. All plugin-added logic is contained: snapshot-service resolution, TryReplace, restore, and notification are each wrapped with catch (Exception) when (exception is not OutOfMemoryException). The worker report records this as a known limitation; it does not defeat the task's requirement that the plugin-added activation/notification never throws, and wrapping base would change host behavior. The tests cover the valid, invalid, snapshot-service-unavailable, and notifier-failing paths.

findings.summary: The bounded 5s wait timeout path is contained by inspection (WaitAsync(TimeSpan) raises TimeoutException, which the catch-all contains) but is not exercised by a unit test; CreateAsync failure and unavailable-manager paths are tested.
findings.detail: JellyfinConfigurationRejectionNotifier.NotifyRejected does activityManager.CreateAsync(entry).WaitAsync(BoundedWait).GetAwaiter().GetResult() inside a catch-all. WaitAsync(TimeSpan) throws TimeoutException when the deadline elapses; the catch contains it and the save path is unaffected. There is no unit test with a never-completing CreateAsync task, so this specific branch is verified by inspection rather than execution. The notifier does not accept a CancellationToken (the host CreateAsync signature has none), so 'cancellation' is not an applicable input path. The tested containment cases are CreateAsync throwing (NotifyRejectedNeverThrowsWhenTheActivityManagerFails) and IActivityManager unavailable (NotifyRejectedDoesNothingWhenTheActivityManagerIsUnavailable).
findings.recommended_action: Optional: add a slow-CreateAsync containment test in a later pass; not required.
